observations: qfourier_g4 improved mean Q.ANT accuracy from qfourier_g2's 0.82253 to 0.82987 while increasing parameters from 31,370 to 62,730; both remain on the Pareto front.
qfourier_g8 did not continue the trend: mean Q.ANT accuracy fell to 0.82103 with 125,450 parameters, so it is dominated and absent from the Pareto front.

h64_512 remained substantially more accurate at 0.85820 with 88,650 parameters; qfourier_g4 therefore retains a parameter advantage but leaves about 2.83 percentage points of mean accuracy on the table.
Mean reference-to-Q.ANT prediction disagreements rose from 274 for g2 to 323 for g4 and 586.7 for g8, while h64_512 averaged only 6.7.

For g8, exact-cosine reference accuracy remained around 0.8365 on average while Q.ANT accuracy averaged 0.8210, indicating that the degradation is not explained solely by failure of the higher-capacity reference model to learn.
interpretation: The capacity hypothesis is only partially supported. Increasing grid size from 2 to 4 improves Q.ANT accuracy and preserves Pareto efficiency, but grid size 8 reverses the gain and sharply increases reference-to-Q.ANT disagreement. This suggests that simply adding higher Fourier frequencies is not a reliable path to closing the ReLU gap under the current exact-cosine-training/Q.ANT-evaluation protocol. The mismatch between the training reference and Q.ANT periodic evaluation becomes more important as grid size grows.
next_research_direction: Prioritize the reference-to-Q.ANT mismatch rather than increasing grid size further. A pre-registered follow-up should test Q.ANT's official training-noise/robustness approach or another Q.ANT-aligned training method at fixed g4 capacity, comparing disagreement and Q.ANT accuracy against the no-noise g4 baseline.
limitations: Q.ANT CPU backend only; no photonic performance claim.
The experiment changes Fourier grid size but not network depth or other architectural dimensions.
